messages:
cheng: Heads up — canary saw a ~3s p95 spike during a scale-up at 12:03 UTC. Correlates with a warm-fork respin/slow-join pattern.
maya: On it. Any traces or profiles yet?
mira: I pulled the perf dump, attaching highlights. joiner wait times jump, plus kernel selection falls back to a slower matmul path. KV hitrate drops simultaneously (92% -> 18%).
sam: KV hitrate to 18% seems extreme. Eviction storm? Which keyspace?
mira: Mostly prefix cache for chat sessions. Evictions line up with fork churn. NVMe IO queue depth spikes at same time.
jordan: Wasn't there a change to kernel scoring weights in last nightly? Could explain fallback.
cheng: Yes — PR #3412 raised latency weight in kernel-scorer to prefer smaller-memory kernels; looks like during fork we ended up picking a fallback kernel that uses an FP16 path with worse throughput on that hw.
oliver: I ran a quick repro with --scale-ramp 200r/s; repro shows joiner backlog ~150ms median, then a long tail while forked workers materialize. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:03:05Z] joiner: waiting_for_fork=3 backlog=48
[2026-03-17T12:03:05Z] kernel-scorer: selected=matmul_fallback_fp16 score=12.4 ctx=512
[2026-03-17T12:03:06Z] kvcache: hitrate=0.18 eviction=high
```

sam: Thanks. So 3 interacting things: fork-respin, nvme contention, kernel scorer pushing fallback. Any quick mitigations?
mira: Quick mitigation that worked in canary: bump warm pool from 1 -> 3 (prewarmed forks). p95 dropped from 3s -> ~120ms.
jordan: Also tried reverting kernel-scorer delta in canary; result: runtime stayed on preferred kernel and throughput recovered even under nvme spikes.
cheng: Action plan: 1) revert the kernel-scorer change in canary (temp rollback), 2) increase canary warmpool to 3 while we validate, 3) gather full perf counters (nvme qd, io latency, joiner histograms) during a controlled ramp, 4) evaluate KV eviction policy and prefix cache sizing.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-034 — Autoscale coldstart latency spike in canary. Severity: P2.
sam: Agree with rollback + warmpool bump. I'll open a short-lived config rollback PR and roll to canary.
oliver: I'll run the controlled ramp with perf counters and upload traces to the incident folder.
mira: Also want to try a hybrid scoring tweak: penalize fallback kernel only when kv_hitrate < 0.5 and io_latency < 3ms. That way scorer is more conservative during noisy IO.
cheng: Good idea. For long-term: consider changing scale policy to keep min_idle=2 for services with heavy prefix-KV dependence, and add a backoff for kernel-score flips during joiner backlog.
jordan: One more note — batching heuristics: current batcher waits up to 8ms for joiner when cold; lowering that to 4ms reduced tail but increased cost a tiny bit. Worth testing.
sam: TL;DR: rollback PR + warmpool bump live in canary, controlled ramp + perf collection in 30m, follow-up postmortem to map root cause and durable remediation.
cheng: Acknowledged. Thanks everyone. I'll post updates in the incident channel and add a short postmortem draft after data collection. :white_check_mark:
